$schema_note: Every sector ranked for THIS buyer: small hands-on investor, $1-2M total cash, natural person, East Coast (DMV core, ME-FL expansion). Scores 1-5 per dimension (5 = best for this buyer). composite = weighted: entry_feasibility x2, yield x1.5, value_add_upside x1.5, regulatory_risk x1 (5 = LOW risk), liquidity x1. Rankings synthesize the per-sector files; every load-bearing number is cited there.

rankings.one_liner: The core: residential debt, verified natural-person exemptions (DC 3-0, PG sourced), 8-14% gross yields in the target metros, and the buyer's hands-on skill is the alpha. Regulatory risk is MANAGED, not absent — the exemptions are the strategy.
rankings.action: Philadelphia first (depth + no rent control), Albany/Scranton for yield, DMV with the exemption playbook, Providence once rents verify.

rankings.one_liner: Secondary-market IOS at 6.75-7.75% (7-10% cash-on-cash) with ZERO residential-style regulation; scarce at the $1-2M ticket but the best risk-adjusted diversifier when found.
rankings.action: Hunt 1-5 acre by-right IOS yards along Richmond/Harrisburg/Allentown corridors via broker networks + tax-sale pipeline.

rankings.one_liner: Class B/C tertiary at 7%+, month-to-month leases, no tenant law, supply falling to 2.4% of stock — the regulatory opposite of multifamily at similar yield.
rankings.action: Screen tertiary East Coast facilities (150-400 units) with third-party management quotes in hand.

rankings.one_liner: Value-add parks at 7-9.5% with the strongest affordability tailwind in housing; East Coast inventory scarcity, PE competition, and spreading MHC-specific tenant statutes temper it.
rankings.action: Before any offer: screen the state's MHC statute (lot-rent notice, sale opportunity-to-purchase) — flagged as a rules-engine gap.

rankings.one_liner: The passive slot: one credit-tenant box at 6.2-6.8%, bond-like, zero regulation — but zero use for the buyer's value-add edge.
rankings.action: Hold as diversification option once the active portfolio is built; necessity-retail tenants only.

rankings.one_liner: 7.3% average caps and anti-institutional politics favor small buyers, but single-tenant vacancy risk and no exemption leverage keep it behind the 2-4 unit core.
rankings.action: Opportunistic only — an SFR next to an owned 2-4 unit compounds the submarket edge.

rankings.one_liner: Highest-margin use of cash (entitlement alpha, no financing contingency) in the same rowhouse submarkets — carried by the core strategy's market knowledge; entitlement risk is the tax.
rankings.action: Off-market/tax-sale lots only, never MLS ask; track NoVA data-center-adjacency dirt as the speculative sleeve.

rankings.one_liner: Near-flagship 2-4 units = the core strategy with a demand floor; purpose-built is institutional and enrollment-cliff-exposed.
rankings.action: Screen College Park (PG rules apply), Richmond/VCU, Newark DE as multifamily deals with an enrollment check.

rankings.one_liner: Only the medical-office edge (6.5-8% stabilized, sticky tenants) is investable at $1-2M; generic office is a leasing-capital trap at this scale.
rankings.action: Passive watch; consider only a hospital-adjacent small MOB with 5+ year tenancy in place.

rankings.one_liner: Hotel fundamentals fine, STR yields real — but the regulatory ratchet in the buyer's urban markets can kill an underwrite with one council vote: the anti-thesis of exemption-anchored certainty.
rankings.action: Avoid urban STR; only writing-verified permissive resort markets qualify, and none screened yet.

rankings.one_liner: Best demographic story in CRE (occupancy records, boomers turn 80) but the product is care operations — not transferable skill. REIT exposure if any.
1.6% vacancy and power-gated growth — two orders of magnitude above budget. The tradeable adjacency is NoVA land (see land_infill).
rankings.action: Intel watch on Loudoun/PW rezonings only.

rankings.one_liner: 23.1% vacancy, half the 2020-25 deliveries still empty; institutional distress story with no small-buyer entry.
Car-wash NNN duplicates the retail slot with worse residual risk; RV/marina/parking are operating businesses. Pass.

portfolio_shape_for_this_buyer: With $1-2M: 60-75% into the 2-4 unit core (2-4 buildings across Philadelphia + one DMV exemption play), 15-25% into ONE diversifier when the right asset surfaces (IOS yard, storage facility, or value-add MHC), 10-15% dry powder for tax-sale/off-market land strikes. Every allocation above assumes natural-person title where exemptions demand it.
